A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BFGS convergence-analysis work. Their main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the reordered Appendices F and G.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original numerical experiments comparing BFGS, gradient descent, and accelerated gradient descent on the hard cubic function and synthetic logistic regression.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G retain these experiments and add computational-cost measurements, step-size trajectories, and affine-transformation experiments.

M1.justification: The BFGS updates, weak Wolfe conditions, and log-bisection line search in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The transformation experiments evaluate the existing algorithm rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The hard cubic and synthetic logistic-regression objectives are retained. Figures 4 and 10 add a specific test scenario involving an ill-conditioned, nonsingular coordinate transformation of the cubic problem.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the two BFGS initializations against gradient descent and accelerated gradient descent. The added experiments reuse these algorithms; the transformed curves represent changed evaluation conditions rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands beyond iteration counts to gradient evaluations and elapsed seconds in Figures 7–8, with dimensions 100, 200, 500, and 1000, and adds paired original/transformed-objective comparisons. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original data-generation recipe, N = d, and Wolfe parameters alpha = 0.1 and beta = 0.9 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New step-size diagnostics in Figures 3 and 9 examine the transition to unit steps, while Figures 4 and 10 test behavior under ill-conditioned coordinate transformations. These add direct investigations of convergence mechanisms and affine invariance beyond the earlier convergence comparisons across dimensions and initializations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing descriptions of random data generation and initialization are retained without new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: The original convergence results are retained, including v1 Figures 3–4 as v2 Figures 5–6. New results show step sizes settling at 1, overlapping original/transformed BFGS trajectories while GD and AGD deteriorate, and eventual BFGS advantages against gradient-evaluation and time budgets. These are additional findings, not improved scores for the original experiments.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.1 and its corollary add a constant 1 and replace log log(1+...) with log(1+log(1+...)) in the line-search bound. Appendix F, formerly G, revises the logistic-regression argument to invoke a bounded sublevel set. The main linear and superlinear convergence theorems remain unchanged, and Appendix E still prints the earlier complexity expression.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: affine-invariant global linear and superlinear BFGS guarantees under strict convexity and strong self-concordance, with arbitrary initial points and positive-definite initial Hessian approximations.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly connects unit-step stabilization to Lemma 4.2 and superlinear convergence, and interprets the transformation results through BFGS's affine invariance. The existing limitation concerning strong rather than standard self-concordance remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 8 newly provides wall-clock optimization-time information. Existing initialization, line-search, and synthetic-data details are retained, but the revision adds no hardware/software specification, transformation-matrix construction, or code-access information.

R1.justification: The revision adds YOR19 as the source of the hard cubic example and replaces the online Q&A footnote supporting log-sum-exp convexity with NH18. The broader positioning against prior BFGS convergence analyses remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include limited copyediting and notation cleanup, updated affiliations, expanded experimental discussion, and swapping the strong-self-concordance and numerical-experiment appendices. The main narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: New step-size, transformation, gradient-evaluation, and timing displays in Figures 3–4 and 7–10 substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing plots are retained with layout adjustments, and v1 Figures 3–4 are relocated and renumbered as Figures 5–6.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics and cost comparisons provide useful empirical support beyond v1's iteration-based plots, and Proposition 5.1's stated bound is corrected. The gains remain limited: Appendix E retains the old formula, the revised logistic-regression argument asserts sublevel-set boundedness without establishing it, and the new timing and transformation experiments lack detailed setup information.
